stories.title: Gencom Divides Into Two Business Lines With Leadership Promotions
stories.excerpt: Real estate investment firm Gencom is reorganizing into two different business lines, with new hires and promotions to match. The reorganization splits the firm, which has $8 billion in assets under management, into Gencom Capital and Gencom Real Estate, with CEO and founder Karim Alibhai continuing to steer both ships, according to Gencom. Gencom operates up to 6,000 hotel rooms nationwide, including brands like Ritz-Carlton, Rosewood, Auberge Resorts Collection, Fairmont, Hyatt and Marriott. “Successful real estate platforms are built by combining disciplined investing with exceptional execution,” Alibhai said in a statement. “As Gencom continues to grow, this evolution strengthens our leadership, sharpens accountability and positions us to capitalize on the opportunities ahead while continuing to deliver outstanding outcomes for our investors and partners.” Gencom Capital will be led by Chief Investment Officer Alessandro Colantonio, who will handle capital markets, portfolio management and capital allocation. Newly promoted managing directors include Ignasi Puig, who will handle acquisitions and investments; Peter Trujillo, who will be responsible for corporate investments; and Blythe Pierre-Louis, who will manage special situations. Meanwhile, Donald McGregor was promoted to president of Gencom Real Estate and will oversee development, construction and asset management. Shaun Johnston was also promoted to head of portfolio finance and accounting and will report directly to McGregor. Jake Lynch was hired as senior vice president of asset management for Gencom Real Estate. “As we continue to grow, we are building a team with the expertise to create value at every stage of the investment lifecycle,” McGregor said in a statement. “Jake is a terrific addition to the Gencom Real Estate platform, and Shaun’s promotion reflects the depth of talent we have developed within the firm. Together, they reinforce our ability to cultivate ta
bullets: Gencom reorganizes $8B AUM into Capital and Real Estate divisions.
Firm operates 6,000 hotel rooms nationally under luxury brands.
Leadership changes strengthen accountability and capital allocation discipline.
stories.summary: Gencom, an $8 billion real estate investor with ~6,000 hotel rooms across luxury brands (Ritz-Carlton, Rosewood, Fairmont, Hyatt, Marriott), is splitting into two business lines: Gencom Capital (led by new Chief Investment Officer Alessandro Colantonio handling capital markets and allocation) and Gencom Real Estate. The reorganization aims to sharpen execution and accountability as the firm scales.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. This is a hotel and diversified real estate firm; the restructuring signals operational maturation and potential capital redeployment, but does not clarify multifamily investment appetite or market-specific demand signals relevant to apartment development underwriting.

stories.title: Landmark Delivers 397-Bed CSU Student Housing Venture
stories.excerpt: Landmark Properties delivered The Mark Fort Collins, a 397-bed off-campus student housing community at 255 Johnson Drive in Fort Collins, less than half a mile from Colorado State University. The project was developed in partnership with Silverpeak Real Estate Partners and Peninsula Investments.  Landmark’s Jason Doornbos added, “Landmark and our joint venture partners took over a stalled project from a previous developer, restarted construction, and delivered a high-quality asset.” The Mark Fort Collins features 193 units in a mix of studio to four-bedroom layouts. Amenities included a heated outdoor pool and sun shelf, a sky deck and lounge, three courtyards, a gaming lawn, multiple firepits with seating areas, a hammock grove, and outdoor grilling spots. The property also features a fitness center, coffee bar, sports simulator, private study and coworking rooms, and a wellness center. bullets: Landmark Properties delivered 397-bed student housing at Fort Collins, Colorado.
Project: 193 units, half-mile from Colorado State University campus.

stories.summary: Landmark Properties, in partnership with Silverpeak Real Estate Partners and Peninsula Investments, completed The Mark Fort Collins, a 397-bed student housing community with 193 units (studio to four-bedroom) located at 255 Johnson Drive, less than half a mile from Colorado State University. Landmark took over a stalled project, restarted construction, and delivered a high-amenity asset featuring a pool, sky deck, gaming lawn, fitness center, and wellness spaces.
stories.impact: Student housing in Fort Collins remains feasible and absorbs readily near CSU; strong execution by Landmark on a repositioned asset signals continued institutional appetite for education-anchored properties in secondary college towns. Colorado Front Range multifamily markets benefit from sustained enrollment and housing scarcity near major universities, supporting rent growth.

stories.title: Real Capital Solutions Launches $350M Distressed Office Acquisition Fund
stories.excerpt: Real Capital Solutions (RCS), a real estate investment firm headquartered in Colorado, has launched a new $350 million fund that will target acquiring distressed Class A and Class B offices across the U.S., Commercial Observer can first report. The fund, RCS Contrarian Office Fund, plans to lever-up and ultimately acquire up to $850 million of office assets from the $350 million raised. The fund is already capitalized through a $50 million personal commitment by Marcel Arsenault, founder and CEO of Real Capital Solutions, and a second $47.5 million commitment from an unnamed entrepreneur. The fund will close in the first quarter of 2027. “While the office market continues to reset, we believe the long-term outlook for premier office assets is extremely strong,” Arsenault said in a statement. “Companies still need high-quality workplaces to attract tenants, foster innovation and drive growth, and those assets will continue to outperform over time.” This is not the first time RCS has jumped into pools of office distress. Since 2024, the firm has invested $644 million into acquiring 14 office properties in 10 U.S. markets — buildings that include Walnut Glen Tower and Tower at Park Lane in Dallas; Belleview Tower in Denver; Tysons Pointe in Northern Virginia; 101 Marietta Street in Atlanta; and the Equitable Building in Chicago, a 35-story Class A office tower the firm acquired earlier this year for $132.5 million, or a 77.8 percent discount to replacement cost. Adam Abeln, chief investment officer and managing director at RCS, credited the firm’s recent investment activity to a “contrarian approach” the firm has always taken, in remarks to CO. “Generally, we found you get rewarded when you have that contrarian outlook where pricing is disconnected from market fundamentals,” he said. “The whole office market today has been painted with the same brush, and the discounts go across the board, regardless if it’s trophy office or Class A, B or C buildings.” The
bullets: Real Capital Solutions launches $350M distressed office acquisition fund.
Fund targets $850M of Class A/B office assets with leverage.
CEO and founder committed $50M; unnamed entrepreneur $47.5M.
stories.summary: Real Capital Solutions (RCS), a Colorado-based real estate firm, launched the RCS Contrarian Office Fund with $350 million in commitments (including $50M from founder Marcel Arsenault and $47.5M from a second investor), targeting acquisition of distressed Class A and Class B office assets nationwide. With leverage, the fund expects to deploy up to $850 million of office capital, betting on long-term institutional demand for premium workplaces.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. However, the aggressive office distress fund launch signals softening office fundamentals and oversupply; institutional capital is rotating to office opportunistically, not to multifamily. This crowds capital away from apartment development and suggests office conversions to residential may accelerate in select markets (NYC, Chicago, other downtowns) if office cap rates spike further and conversion spreads narrow.

stories.title: El-Ad National Buys Oceanfront Fort Lauderdale Hotel for $60M
stories.excerpt: Developer El-Ad National Properties has paid $60 million for an oceanfront hotel in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., property records show. The 99-room Sea Club Resort sits on a 1.2-acre site at 619 North Fort Lauderdale Beach Boulevard, between Belmar and Auramar streets. The 54,982-square-foot building dates back to 1954. An entity tied to Rachel Levy and Michael Man has owned the resort since 1995, when it paid just under $4 million for it. The entity provided $40 million in seller financing to El-Ad National Properties, a Boca Raton-based division of Israeli billionaire Isaac Tshuva’s El-Ad Group. The property will likely be redeveloped. Berkadia has been marketing the site as “one of the last remaining oceanfront development sites in the Fort Lauderdale area.” The land is zoned to house a 541-unit, 246,989-square-foot development up to 200 feet tall, according to Berkadia. An additional 40 feet could be granted if 60 percent of units serve as a hotel, though the Sea Club Resort’s lobby is protected under a preservation agreement with the Broward Trust for Historic Preservation. El-Ad is an active developer in South Florida. Last year, it nabbed an $85 million construction loan for a mixed-use, 2.8 million-square-foot development in Davie. That same year, it completed the luxury Alina Residences condo development in Boca Raton. A spokesperson for El-Ad did not respond to a request for comment. The sellers could not be reached for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: El-Ad National bought oceanfront Fort Lauderdale hotel for $60M.
Sea Club Resort: 99 rooms, 1.2 acres, 1954-vintage property.
Zoned for 541-unit, 247K-sf mixed-use development up to 200 feet.
stories.summary: El-Ad National Properties (Boca Raton division of Israeli billionaire Isaac Tshuva's El-Ad Group) acquired the oceanfront Sea Club Resort in Fort Lauderdale for $60 million with $40 million in seller financing. The 99-room, 54,982-sf property sits on 1.2 acres at a prime oceanfront location. The land is zoned to support a 541-unit, 246,989-sf mixed-use development up to 200 feet (240 feet with 60% hotel component); the resort's historic lobby is protected.
stories.impact: South Florida development: El-Ad's acquisition signals confidence in Fort Lauderdale beachfront redevelopment and potential residential upside. The 541-unit entitlement and oceanfront scarcity create a rare dense multifamily-plus-hotel play; soft-landing zoning and significant deferred maintenance on a low-value hotel create conversion/redevelopment arbitrage. This is likely a ground-up replacement rather than adaptive reuse, supporting aggressive absorption assumptions in South Florida coastal markets.

stories.title: Oxbow Adding 10 Retail Buildings to Pearl Project
stories.excerpt: Oxbow Development Group submitted plans to the city for 10 new retail buildings on either side of Avenue A. Along with completely new builds, the firm is seeking permission to demolish a vacant industrial building at 250 E. Grayson St.,. The new structures will add 85,000 square feet of space to the complex. The development is being led in a partnership between Oxbow and 3-O Real Estate Partners. The San Antonio Business Journal reports the joint venture is aiming for a mix of local, regional, national and global tenants that are a good fit for Pearl. Alamo Architects and Don B. McDonald Architects are designing the project. Oxbow plans to break ground in early 2027, expecting to finish construction in late 2028. Pearl Brewery Redevelopment features the transformational adaptive reuse of a 21-acre 1900s brewery into a mixed-use village. bullets: Oxbow Development adds 10 retail buildings, 85K sf to Pearl Project.
San Antonio Pearl Brewery: 21-acre mixed-use adaptive reuse village.
Groundbreaking early 2027; completion targeted late 2028.
stories.summary: Oxbow Development Group (partnering with 3-O Real Estate Partners) submitted plans to demolish a vacant industrial building and add 10 new retail structures totaling 85,000 sf on both sides of Avenue A within the Pearl Brewery redevelopment in San Antonio. The 21-acre adaptive reuse village project targets a mix of local, regional, national, and global retailers and is slated to break ground early 2027 and deliver by late 2028.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. Pearl Brewery is primarily retail and adaptive reuse; however, mixed-use activation and the multi-year build timeline signal sustained consumer demand and long-term rental fundamentals in San Antonio's central neighborhoods. If Pearl's success drives residential demand nearby, apartment developers should monitor future phases and consider infill multifamily sites in the Pearl/south downtown corridor.

stories.title: Bezos’ Aerospace Company Could Land in Hutto
stories.excerpt: Construction of a manufacturing plant associated with Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin aerospace company may soon be a reality for Hutto, joining a host of other Central Texas spaceflight companies. The proposed Project Blue Hub plant will be about the size of 26 football fields – 1.3 million square feet at a cost of $650 million. It would be joining a host of other Central Texas spaceflight companies. Blue Origin is a competitor to Elon Musk’s SpaceX project, located in nearby Bastrop. The towns economic development agency has been working on financial incentives, should Blue Origin commit. If plans come to fruition, the deal could bring up to 2,000 jobs to the area. Blue Origin was established by Bezos in 2000 The post Bezos’ Aerospace Company Could Land in Hutto appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Blue Origin proposes 1.3M-sf manufacturing plant in Hutto, Texas.
Project Blue Hub: $650M investment, targets ~2,000 skilled jobs.
Plant comparable to 26 football fields; location near Bastrop/SpaceX.
stories.summary: Blue Origin (Jeff Bezos' aerospace company) is exploring a manufacturing plant in Hutto, Texas—Project Blue Hub—a 1.3 million square-foot facility with an estimated $650 million investment expected to create nearly 2,000 skilled jobs. Hutto's economic development agency is pursuing financial incentives. The facility would join other Central Texas spaceflight companies, including SpaceX in nearby Bastrop.
stories.impact: Austin metro/Hutto demand driver: A 2,000-job Blue Origin facility would inject significant wage-earning population into the northern Austin exurb, accelerating commute-shed demand for workforce housing in Hutto, Pflugerville, and Round Rock. Multifamily developers should monitor lease-up timelines and project financing; a 2026–2027 operational ramp would support Class B/C apartment starts in the I-35 corridor 2024–2025. This is a material population pull for Central Texas if finalized.

stories.title: Town Lane, Axis Partners Launch IOS Platform Venture
stories.excerpt: Town Lane, a New York-based real estate investment management firm, has acquired a 23-property industrial outdoor storage (IOS) portfolio and launched a platform venture with Axis Partners, an Atlanta-based industrial owner and operator. The transaction includes an investment by Town Lane in the Axis operating platform. Terms were not disclosed. The portfolio comprises mission-critical, infill IOS assets that support the day-to-day operations of local, regional, and national businesses, including contractors, equipment rental companies, distributors, infrastructure providers, and service businesses. It’s located in high-growth Sunbelt markets such as Atlanta, Houston, Dallas and Nashville. “The Axis team has built a differentiated sourcing and operating platform that consistently identifies mission-critical, off-market assets supporting the infrastructure behind local and regional economies,” said Garret Overlock, managing director at Town Lane. “This partnership provides a unique opportunity to combine institutional capital with an experienced operator, and we’re excited to build a market-leading platform together over the long term.” Pictured: An Axis Partners-owned IOS facility in Laredo, TX. The post Town Lane, Axis Partners Launch IOS Platform Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Town Lane acquires 23-property industrial outdoor storage portfolio.
Platform JV with Axis Partners; assets in Atlanta, Houston, Dallas, Nashville.
Mission-critical infill IOS supporting contractors, equipment rental, distributors.
stories.summary: Town Lane (New York-based real estate investment manager) acquired a 23-property industrial outdoor storage (IOS) portfolio and launched a platform venture with Axis Partners (Atlanta-based industrial operator). The portfolio comprises mission-critical, infill IOS assets serving contractors, equipment rental companies, distributors, and service businesses across high-growth Sunbelt markets (Atlanta, Houston, Dallas, Nashville). Terms undisclosed; Town Lane made an investment in the Axis operating platform.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. IOS is non-housing; however, the capital deployment in Sunbelt industrial by institutional investors signals strong fundamentals in gateway metros (Houston, Atlanta, Dallas, Nashville). These markets are also hot for apartment development; strong industrial/logistics ecosystems underpin job growth and wage profiles that support multifamily rent growth and absorption in these submarkets.

stories.title: James Marcellino Re-Joins Colliers’ New York City Office as Vice President
stories.excerpt: More than 13 years after departing Colliers as an associate director, James Marcellino has returned to the company’s New York office as a vice president. Starting today, Aug. 10, , Marcellino’s new role will focus on office leasing and tenant representation as Colliers continues expanding its New York presence, according to an announcement by the firm. John Gallagher, executive managing director for New York City at Colliers, called Marcellino’s return “another important step” in the firm’s growth. “His institutional ownership experience and entrepreneurial perspective will bring immediate value to our clients and our team, and we’re thrilled to welcome him back,” Gallagher said in a statement. The executive brings with him more than 17 years of experience advising institutional owners, landlords and occupiers on office leasing. In his most recent work as a real estate consultant, Marcellino advised the Bracha Group, Modernus Architectural Products, and Christie’s International Real Estate’s leading residential sales team, the Gottlieb Team. Marcellino previously served as vice president of leasing at L&L Holding Company from 2023 to 2024, according to the announcement. While there, he oversaw leasing strategy for its 6.3 million-square-foot portfolio and completed nearly 344,000 square feet of office and retail transactions. Marcellino first arrived at Colliers as an associate director in late 2011. bullets: James Marcellino rejoins Colliers NYC as Vice President.
Focus: office leasing and tenant representation in Manhattan.
Brings 17+ years institutional owner/landlord/occupier experience.
stories.summary: James Marcellino, after 13+ years away, has re-joined Colliers' New York City office as Vice President effective Aug. 10, focusing on office leasing and tenant representation. He brings 17+ years advising institutional owners, landlords, and occupiers on office transactions, with recent experience at L&L Holding Company and as a consultant to firms like Bracha Group and Modernus.
stories.impact: Minimal impact on multifamily development. Marcellino's hire signals Colliers' continued emphasis on Manhattan office leasing amid market softness; his institutional ownership background may support office-to-residential conversion advisory, but the hire does not indicate new multifamily demand or supply signals in NYC markets.

stories.title: Westville To Open at 540 Third Avenue in Murray Hill
stories.excerpt: Westville is getting ready to open its 12th location in the U.S. and bring a selection of classic American foods to Manhattan’s Murray Hill neighborhood. The restaurant brand just signed a 4,148-square-foot lease at the base of 540 Third Avenue, also known as the Dian, a 22-story, 160-unit residential building at the corner of Third Avenue and East 36th Street, according to broker Meridian Capital Group. The lease comprises 2,739 square feet on the ground floor and 1,409 square feet on the lower level. The asking rent and the length of the lease were not disclosed, but the average asking rent for retail space in the nearby Herald Square area was $394 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. CBRE’s Robert Bonicoro and Betsy Da Silva represented Westville in the lease, while Meridian’s James Famularo and Jordan Langer represented ownership, which is a joint venture between Gilar Realty and Ranco Capital. CBRE did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. “Westville had its pick of locations in this market, and its decision to commit long-term at 540 Third Avenue underscores the continued demand for well-built, well-located retail on Third Avenue,” Langer said in a statement. Meridian did not disclose when Westville will open its new Murray Hill location. The franchise also has Manhattan restaurants in the West Village, Chelsea, the East Village, the Upper East Side and on Wall Street, as well as a spot in Long Island City, Queens. Westville opened its first location outside of New York City in Northern Virginia. “When Whole Foods and Westville commit to the same few blocks within months of each other, that is not a coincidence, it is a corridor being repositioned in real time,” Famularo said in a statement. “Ownership delivered a first-class space and held firm on value, and we brought in an operator that will draw customers from the day it opens.”
bullets: Westville restaurant opens 12th U.S. location at 540 Third Avenue, Manhattan.
Lease: 4,148 sf (2,739 ground floor, 1,409 lower level), Murray Hill.
440 Third Avenue (the Dian): 22-story, 160-unit residential building.
stories.summary: Westville, a classic American restaurant brand, signed a 4,148-sf ground and lower-level lease at 540 Third Avenue (the Dian) in Manhattan's Murray Hill neighborhood for its 12th U.S. location. The mixed-use building (160 residential units, 22 stories) sits at the corner of Third Avenue and East 36th Street. Asking rent and lease term not disclosed; Herald Square-area retail averaged $394/sf in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal impact on multifamily development. Retail ground-floor leasing in NYC—even at mixed-use residential buildings—reflects restaurant operator confidence in neighborhood foot traffic, not apartment demand signals. However, the Dian's 160-unit residential component and leasing activity in Murray Hill suggest steady renter traffic; no supply or demand surprise here.

stories.title: Bristol Myers Squibb Chooses Houston for $2.3B Investment
stories.excerpt: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) selected Houston as the site for a new, multi-modal manufacturing campus, representing an approximately $2.3 billion investment designed to accelerate the delivery of next-generation medicines to patients. The campus, at Generation Park in Houston, will create nearly 500 skilled jobs and is designed to grow in scale, capability and workforce for decades to come. The selection of Houston marks a significant milestone in BMS’ $40 billion commitment to invest in the United States over five years across research and development, technology and domestic manufacturing. The Houston campus will be modular and multi-modal. Its modular design allows BMS to add and reconfigure manufacturing capacity as needed, reflecting BMS’ current and future pipeline. Its multi-modal capabilities allow BMS to manufacture multiple types of medicines – such as small molecules, biologics, and antibody-drug conjugates – across a range of disease areas. Last year, Eli Lilly announced it would invest in a $6.5 billion active pharmaceutical ingredients plant, also in the Generation Park complex in Houston. The post Bristol Myers Squibb Chooses Houston for $2.3B Investment appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Bristol Myers Squibb commits $2.3B manufacturing campus in Houston.
Generation Park location; ~500 skilled jobs, modular/multi-modal design.
Part of $40B U.S. investment over five years across R&D and manufacturing.
stories.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) selected Houston's Generation Park for a new $2.3 billion multi-modal manufacturing campus creating nearly 500 skilled jobs. The modular campus allows BMS to scale manufacturing capacity for small molecules, biologics, and antibody-drug conjugates. This investment is part of BMS' broader $40 billion, five-year U.S. commitment to R&D, technology, and domestic manufacturing. Last year, Eli Lilly announced a $6.5 billion API plant in the same Generation Park complex.
stories.impact: Houston metro demand driver: BMS's $2.3B campus and 500-job commitment, coupled with Eli Lilly's $6.5B API plant at Generation Park, signal major life sciences agglomeration and wage-earner migration into northwest Houston. Multifamily developers should prioritize Class A apartment supply near Generation Park and along I-290/Beltway 8 northwest corridor; skilled manufacturing and biotech jobs command premium rents and support absorption velocity. A 2-3 year operational ramp creates a window to deliver workforce housing in 2025–2026.
